mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically across four consecutive weekly means (-1.6, -0.4, -0.1, +0.3). This momentum is slow-moving and self-propagating, so the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days will exceed the last 28-day mean of -0.45.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly means rise monotonically from -1.6 to +0.3 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC prints below -0.45, i.e. the four-week upward drift reverses rather than continues.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT sits at only +0.6, still well short of its pre-pandemic level, and has been pinned in the 0.6-0.7 band for three weeks. A crossing above +1.5 marks full resumption of discretionary trip-making, which precedes a lift in RETAIL_REC by up to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above +1.5 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly means are 0.7, 0.6, 0.6 over t-2w to t-0w, holding below +1.0
regime_hint: reopening with transit still below baseline
failure_condition: Within four weeks of TRANSIT first printing above +1.5, the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly high WORKPLACES (+4.3) and improving PARKS (-10.6 to -6.7) mark a coordinated return to out-of-home routines; the pairing multiplies weekday commuting and weekend leisure footfall more than either series alone, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean at or above +4.0 while PARKS improves for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improves from -10.6 to -6.7 while WORKPLACES holds at 4.3-4.7
failure_condition: Conditional on WORKPLACES >= +4.0 and two consecutive PARKS improvements, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean is equal to or lower than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM remains more than 40 points above baseline but is drifting down (44.4 to 42.9). Each point of grocery-trip reallocation releases household time and spend into discretionary channels, so a break below 43.0 precedes higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declines from 44.4 to 42.9 across t-2w to t-0w
regime_hint: steady state with elevated but decaying grocery substitution
failure_condition: A GROCERY_PHARM print below 43.0 is not followed within two weeks by a RETAIL_REC weekly mean above its value in the triggering week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has slipped from 4.0 to 3.7, a small but consistent exit from home. Fewer hours at home convert directly into additional discretionary trips, so the decline lifts RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declines 4.0 to 3.7 while RETAIL_REC rises to +0.3
failure_condition: A RESIDENTIAL print below 3.8 is not followed within one week by a RETAIL_REC weekly mean at or above +0.3.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-November opens the year-end shopping window, and the concurrent improvement in PARKS (-10.6 to -6.7) shows outdoor leisure demand building. That same demand channel carries into discretionary retail, raising RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS weekly means improve from -10.6 to -6.7 into the third week of November
regime_hint: year-end seasonal window with no new restrictions
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the prior 28-day mean while PARKS remains above -9 throughout the window.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM stuck above 42 combined with WORKPLACES plateauing near +4.3 shows household caution is not unwinding. With RETAIL_REC already at +0.3 there is no headroom, so the next two weeks mean-revert lower.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 42.0 and WORKPLACES stays below +5.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM 43.1 to 42.9 and WORKPLACES 4.4 to 4.3 are flat over t-1w to t-0w
regime_hint: pandemic steady state with residual caution
failure_condition: The next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the prior 28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM stays above 42.0 and WORKPLACES stays below +5.0.

mechanism_narrative: The joint normalization of TRANSIT (+0.6), WORKPLACES (+4.3) and PARKS (-6.7 and improving) is the signature of an active relaxation regime with no re-tightening. Policy-driven reopening propagates to discretionary retail with a roughly four-week lag.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT, WORKPLACES and PARKS are all flat or improving week-on-week, indicating no new restriction shock
evidence_refs: fact:all three series are flat to improving across t-3w to t-0w
regime_hint: post-relaxation reopening with no new restrictions announced
failure_condition: TRANSIT, WORKPLACES and PARKS all remain non-deteriorating, yet the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the prior 28-day mean, rejecting the lagged-reopening mechanism.
